name: etcd
tagline: Raft-based, strongly consistent key-value store that holds Kubernetes' cluster state.
description: etcd is a small, strongly consistent key-value store designed for the most critical data in a distributed system: configuration, service discovery, leader election and locks. It replicates via Raft, keeps a multi-version history so clients can watch for changes from any revision, and attaches leases to keys for TTL-based expiry. Every Kubernetes control plane depends on it, which makes it one of the most widely deployed databases in the world even if few people query it directly. Keep datasets small (the default quota is 2 GB, recommended maximum about 8 GB); it is a coordination service, not a general-purpose database.

pricing.notes: Free; managed implicitly as part of every managed Kubernetes control plane.

scale.notes: Every member stores the full dataset; clusters of 3 or 5 members are typical. Designed for gigabytes, not terabytes.

strengths: Linearizable reads and writes through Raft consensus
Watch API streams changes from any historical revision
Leases, locks and leader election primitives built in
Battle-tested as the backing store of every Kubernetes cluster
Simple single binary with TLS and RBAC
weaknesses: Full dataset on every member, with a recommended ceiling of about 8 GB
Write throughput bounded by a single Raft leader and disk fsync latency
Not meant for application data or large values
useCases: Feature flags and small metadata for infrastructure
